description: Estudiante de Ingeniería de Sistemas. Busco personas con conocimientos en programación, diseño, datos o comunicación, con ganas de colaborar y aportar al proyecto.
summary:
HORIZON: Aurora-1 is an educational exploration and survival game for children aged 7–12, developed by SPAGHETTIFICATION for the NASA Space Apps challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.”

Players manage a research base on Mars, balancing energy, oxygen, food, and radiation shielding. Each decision affects connected systems: increasing greenhouse lighting can improve food production, but leaves less electricity for other essential equipment.

The game combines 3D exploration, first-person repairs, and a scientific mystery across a ten-sol campaign. The first three sols provide guided training with ASTROBOT, a robotic companion. Players then face emergencies, investigate clues, and observe the consequences of their choices. Exploration continues after the story ends.

The project integrates NASA DONKI for solar activity records, the NASA Image and Video Library API for real scientific photographs, and APOD for astronomical images and explanations. Documented observations are clearly distinguished from the fictional colony and simulated resource effects.

Built with TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Next.js, and Three.js, HORIZONTE aims to make engineering trade-offs understandable and engaging, helping children develop curiosity and scientific thinking.
details: Horizon: AstroColony is an educational video game in which children explore a colony on Mars and make decisions to keep their crew alive. They can explore the base in 3D, enter its modules, talk to robots, and complete missions while managing energy, oxygen, food, and protection. Every decision has consequences, which helps them gain a hands-on understanding of the challenges of living off-Earth and develop scientific curiosity and critical thinking. The project incorporates NASA data on solar activity to connect the experience to real-world data; the science fiction elements are presented as part of the story. We developed it as a web application using Next.js, React, TypeScript, WebGL, Prisma, and PostgreSQL, and deployed it on Vercel. Our approach combines exploration, storytelling, and learning into an experience accessible via a web browser, prioritizing clear controls, easy-to-understand missions, and engagement for audiences of all ages.
